/whyTourWorks/routeLogicSections/0/items.source_en: The afternoon is bundled into two blocks walked with the van parked

⟦G0⟧ and the Choi Family House are a 10–15 minute riverside walk from Woljeonggyo along the Namcheon, and Daereungwon and Hwangnidan-gil are separated by a single wall. So instead of four stops for four places we make only two drop-offs — the time that used to go into boarding and unboarding becomes walking time, and each block gets 75 minutes.
The season decides the last slot — museum or night view

From March to October we reach ⟦G0⟧ at about 17:00 (30 minutes ahead of its 17:30 last admission). From November to February the sun is already going down at that same hour, so we drive five minutes to Donggung & Wolji instead and watch it from dusk through to the moment the lights come on. It is a picture the summer timetable cannot make.
See it at the tomb, then see it again at the museum

You stand at the 1973 excavation site inside Cheonmachong at Daereungwon, and then meet the actual Cheonmachong Gold Crown (National Treasure No. 188) from that tomb at the next stop, ⟦G0⟧. The same goes for the 33,000-plus artifacts in the Wolji Hall — they came out of the bed of the pond at Donggung & Wolji, the winter alternate. The order itself does the explaining.
Every pickup point is a subway station exit

Busan Station Exit 4 (Line 1), Seomyeon Station Exit 4 (Lines 1 & 2), Haeundae Station Exit 5 (Line 2). At Busan Station in particular, we meet at Exit 4 of the subway station in front of the building, not inside the KTX railway terminal — the train station plaza mixes buses and taxis and makes a vehicle hard to find, while a subway exit number is something anyone finds in one go. Drop-off is at the same three points.
Mini-van size, between a coach and a private car

Coach tours from Busan carry 35–45 passengers cheaply; private tours carry 1–4 at a much higher rate. This small-group mini-van sits between the two — fewer people means faster reassembly at each stop, and that time turns straight back into time on site.

/whyTourWorks/routeLogicSections/0/title.source_en: Why this route is built this way

/routeShapeIntro/subtitle.source_en: A year-round day trip that starts in Busan and walks Gyeongju in a single day. The morning is two places reached by road (⟦G1⟧ and Bulguksa); the afternoon is two blocks walked with the van parked — from ⟦G2⟧ and the Choi Family House across the Namcheon to Woljeonggyo, and from the Daereungwon tombs over one wall into Hwangnidan-gil. The last slot belongs to the season: March to October it is ⟦G0⟧, where the actual crown from the tomb you just walked through is on display, and November to February that same hour is the night-view hour, so it becomes Donggung & Wolji. Built for travellers who care less about how many sights they ticked off than about how long they got to stay at each one.
